claims.statement: For the governed half-skew BSSC P, let M_n(P) be the unnormalized private-message Marton sum functional of the n-fold product channel P^{\otimes n}, in bits per n-use super-symbol. Applying Marton's one-letter coding theorem to that super-channel and normalizing the resulting blocklength proves C_sum(P) >= M_n(P)/n for every n >= 1. Independent concatenation proves M_{m+n}(P) >= M_m(P)+M_n(P); since 0 <= M_n(P) <= 2n bits, Fekete's lemma gives C_sum(P) >= lim_{n->infinity} M_n(P)/n = sup_{n>=1} M_n(P)/n. If L_RTD denotes the exact randomized-time-division value, equivalently the established one-letter binary-input Marton value M_1(P), then a certified n-letter Marton witness of value S_n strictly improves the one-letter Marton lower bound through this super-symbol normalization if and only if S_n > n L_RTD, and k independent copies propagate that gain to blocklength kn with value k S_n. At n=2 the exact threshold is 2 L_RTD, whose governed 33-decimal display begins 0.723285768843909231326883156301174. Equality M_n(P)=n L_RTD at any fixed n is not a capacity converse. The displayed decimal is a prefix, so a rigorous strict comparison must use the exact variational definition of L_RTD or a directed upper enclosure rather than treating the prefix as an exact upper bound.
